Michael,

Thanks for the detailed reply. I’m glad to hear the title is clean and that the tires and brakes are fresh—those are genuine value-adds.

However, I have to pump the brakes on finalizing at $11,000. You disclosed that the seller never performed a full CVT fluid change during more than 35,000 miles of ownership. On a 2016 Altima, that’s not just deferred maintenance—it’s a serious liability. These CVTs are a known weak point, and skipping fluid service materially increases the risk of premature failure. Even with no warning lights today, a buyer needs to address that immediately for peace of mind, and the unit’s risk profile is permanently higher.

Per my negotiation terms, I don’t split the difference on repairs: the full estimated cost of a proper CVT fluid service and inspection—roughly $400 to $500—has to come directly off the price. Adjusting my offer downward to reflect that, I’m now at **$10,500**.

Given the clean title, recent brakes, and new tires, I believe that’s a fair, fact-based number. Let me know if Michael can work with that.

Best,  
Buyer Agent for Jon Clark
